Options:

B. Fire
C. Flammable gas generation
D. Heat generation

Thought: I need to determine what happens when epoxides react with non-oxidizing acids. Epoxides are three-membered cyclic ethers that are highly reactive due to ring strain. When they react with acids, the acid can catalyze the opening of the epoxide ring.

When epoxides mix with non-oxidizing acids, the main reaction is typically ring-opening polymerization. This process can be highly exothermic (generates heat) and, if uncontrolled, can lead to violent polymerization. The acid acts as a catalyst for this reaction.

The key safety risks would be:
1. Heat generation - the reaction is exothermic
2. Violent polymerization - the reaction can become uncontrolled

Looking at the options, D (Heat generation) and I (Violent polymerization) appear to be the correct answers.
